Advancing Women's Health to Improve Outcomes in All Phases of Life (executive order)

status_summary: Executive Order 14182, signed 2025-01-24, revoked Executive Orders 14076 and 14079 of 2022, the orders on access to reproductive healthcare services. The HHS strategic plan page, read on 2026-10-18, still presents the 2022 to 2026 plan with an updated plan described as forthcoming and no conception-to-natural-death language. No source read confirms that the HHS task force was disbanded, that a pro-life task force was installed, or that a Special Representative for Domestic Women's Health was created. An executive order of 2026-10-19 on women's health replaces the 2024 research order with a White House Women's Health Task Force and an NIH Women's Health Division; it is a women's health structure of a different kind from the Special Representative the Mandate names and carries no conception-to-natural-death language.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14182 (Enforcing the Hyde Amendment) revoked Executive Orders 14076 and 14079, the 2022 orders on reproductive healthcare access.

The President signs the executive order Advancing Women's Health to Improve Outcomes in All Phases of Life: it directs HHS, through the NIH Director, to establish a Women's Health Division within 90 days, creates a White House Women's Health Task Force co-chaired by the HHS Secretary and the White House Chief of Staff, and revokes Executive Order 14120 of 2024 and the 2023 memorandum on the women's health research initiative; the order text contains no conception-to-natural-death or pro-life language and does not create a Special Representative for Domestic Women's Health.

title: Replace HHS reproductive access task force with a pro-life task force and mission language
uncertainties: Executive Order 14182 was re-read on federalregister.gov in review: signed 2025-01-24 (90 FR 8751), Sec. 2 revokes Executive Orders 14076 and 14079 and the order does not mention HHS, a task force or a strategic plan. The HHS strategic plan page on hhs.gov is labeled 2022 to 2026 with an updated plan described as forthcoming and contains no conception-to-natural-death language. Federal Register API searches since 2025-01-20 for the task force name and, in review, for HHS documents mentioning a pro-life task force returned zero documents. Internal HHS task force records, staff pages and any women's health representative appointment would not appear in these sources, so the record rests on absence of evidence; the Unified Agenda, Congress and news checks of a full systematic review were not run. Revoking the underlying orders is not confirmation that an HHS-level task force was eliminated. The women's health executive order of 2026-10-19 was read on whitehouse.gov; it is recorded as a parallel step on the women's health element only, and its Federal Register citation was not yet available on 2026-10-20.
